RL на реальных роботах и дообучение VLA: RL on real robots and VLA fine-tuning
Ада едет от кровати к плите 12 шагов, на: Ada drives from the bed to the stove in 12 steps, and the only reward is at the stove: +10, γ = 0.9. How does the return G_t change from the bed to the stove?
Растёт степенно: у кровати 3,14, и кажды: It grows along powers of γ: 3.14 at the bed, and each step toward the stove divides it by 0.9
Растёт по прямой от 0 у кровати до 10 у: It grows along a straight line from 0 at the bed to 10 at the stove
Везде равна 10: награду Ада получит в лю: It equals 10 everywhere: Ada will get the reward either way
Если вся награда приходит у плиты, кажды: If the whole reward comes at the stove, each step back from it multiplies the return by γ: at the bed it is 10 · 0.9¹¹ = 3.14, and three steps before the stove, 8.1. A straight line instead of the power curve gave the forecast a mean error of 0.59. At γ = 0.5, only 0.005 is left at the bed: the weight of the reward halves with every step.
Отдача и дисконт: почему будущее весит м: Return and discounting: why the future weighs less
Ада с γ = 0,99 объезжает лужу (−1) у мой: With γ = 0.99, Ada drives around the puddle (−1) by the sink: the detour around the kitchen table is two steps longer. Which of these will make her drive through the puddle?
Поднять награду у плиты выше 50,8, сдела: Raising the stove reward above 50.8, making each step cost more than 0.412 or making the puddle cost less than 0.197
Ничего: при γ = 0,99 она объезжает лужу: Nothing: at γ = 0.99, she drives around the puddle whatever the rewards
Через лужу выгоднее, если Rγ(1 − γ²) > p: Going through the puddle pays if Rγ(1 − γ²) > p: the two extra steps cost Ada a share 1 − γ² of the reward, and that share is compared with the penalty. At γ = 0.99, it is 2% of 10, less than the penalty of 1, so she takes the detour. For the impatient Ada with γ = 0.5, the same two steps cost 75% of the reward, and she drives through the puddle: 12 steps instead of 14.
У привычной Ады, которую научили по демо: Ada was taught to drive from demonstrations, and in all 70 cells the action she chooses by habit has an advantage A(s, a) = 0. What does this tell you?
Ни о чём, кроме того, что V^π(s) и есть: Nothing, except that V^π(s) is exactly Q^π(s, π(s)): the advantage compares an action with the habitual behavior rather than judging the action in itself
Что привычный маршрут оптимален: улучшит: That the habitual route is optimal and can't be improved
Что привычные действия бесполезны: после: That the habitual actions are useless: the return doesn't grow after them
Маршрут привычной Ады — 18 шагов вместо: Ada's habitual route takes 18 steps instead of 12, and still her own actions have A = 0, while 17 other actions have a positive advantage: “right” in cell (4, 2), for example, has +1.20. This one switch shortens the route to 14 steps, and policy iteration brings it down to 12 in 6 rounds and raises the return at the bed from 1.67 to 3.14, the same as value iteration.
Преимущество: насколько действие лучше о: Advantage: how much better an action is than usual
Робот в настоящей квартире не знает табл: A robot in a real apartment doesn't know the transition table and learns values from experience. It always chooses the action with the largest current estimate. What happens to the route around the kitchen table?
Робот может его не найти: первые попытки: The robot may never find it: its first tries at turning that way give little, and it stops turning there, so it needs a share of random actions
Он найдёт его так же, как итерация ценно: It finds it just as value iteration does: the Bellman equation is the same
Он найдёт его быстрее: опыт точнее модел: It finds it faster: experience is more accurate than a model
Итерация ценности — планирование по изве: Value iteration is planning with a known model; learning from experience also requires exploration. On Sutton and Barto's problem with ten options, the greedy strategy found the best one in only about a third of the cases, and its average reward leveled off at about 1 when 1.54 was possible; with ε = 0.1, the best option was found sooner. DQN started with ε = 1 and lowered it to 0.1 over the first million frames.
Исследование и использование: зачем иног: Exploration and exploitation: why it sometimes pays to drive the wrong way
REINFORCE подталкивает каждое действие с: REINFORCE pushes up every action taken, with the return after it as the weight. In Ada's corridor, she gets +1 for every meter toward the kitchen, and the drive ended in a crash. Which steering decisions will the update push up?
Почти все: отдача положительна на 49 шаг: Almost all of them: the return is positive at 49 of 68 steps, so good and bad decisions alike get pushed up, only with different strength
Только решения в начале поездки, когда д: Only the decisions at the start of the drive, when the crash was still far away
Ни одно: поездка неудачная, отдача отриц: None: the drive failed, so the return is negative
Награда за продвижение делает отдачу поч: A reward for progress makes the return almost always positive, and the signal drowns in noise. Subtracting the value V(s), the baseline, turns the return into an advantage that takes both signs: in the same drive, at 22 steps the return is positive while the GAE advantage is negative, and the wrong turns get pushed down long before the impact.
Базовая линия и преимущество: сравнивать: Baseline and advantage: comparing with the usual
Две Ады учатся ехать на кухню с одним ша: Two Adas learn to drive to the kitchen with the same Adam step size of 0.003 and 5 epochs over each rollout batch. One learns without clipping, the other with PPO, ε = 0.2. What happens after 50 updates?
Без обрезки — ни одной поездки до кухни: Without clipping, not one of 400 drives reaches the kitchen; PPO gets 295, and 99% in the last ten updates
Без обрезки научится быстрее: её шаги бо: The one without clipping learns faster: her steps are larger
Обе научатся одинаково: обрезка только э: Both learn equally well: clipping only saves compute
Обновления без обрезки меняли политику в: Updates without clipping changed the policy dozens of times more: a median KL per update of 0.29 versus 0.0095, and the largest jump was 3.6. After such a jump, the next drives are made by a different policy, and the advantages don't apply to it. A small step size of 0.0003 prevents the jumps but learns slowly: 48% versus 99%.
Две Ады учатся ехать на кухню: без обрез: Two Adas learn to drive to the kitchen: without clipping and with PPO
Расставь по порядку, что происходит за о: Put in order what happens during one PPO training cycle in Ada's corridor.
Поездки: Ада проезжает 8 поездок текущей: Drives: Ada makes 8 drives with the current policy, and the starts and the random steering are recorded
Критик и GAE: критик оценивает ценность: Critic and GAE: the critic estimates the value of each state, and the advantages are computed from the rewards
Эпохи: 5 проходов мини-пакетами по 128 ш: Epochs: 5 passes in minibatches of 128 steps, with the probability ratio clipped at 1 ± 0.2
Порция опыта выбрасывается: следующие по: The rollout batch is discarded: the next drives are made by the updated policy
Так PPO остаётся on-policy: порция опыта: This is how PPO stays on-policy: a rollout batch lives for a few epochs and is discarded, because the policy gradient holds only near the policy that collected the data. In the lesson's diagram, the number of drives out of 8 that reached the kitchen was 0, 3, 7 and 8 at updates 1, 10, 20 and 50; Rudin et al. ran 1,500 such cycles, with 4,096 × 24 steps in each.
Почему большой шаг портит политику: дове: Why a large step ruins the policy: the trust region and clipping
У Rudin и соавторов порция опыта — 4096: In Rudin et al.'s setup, a rollout batch is 4,096 robots with 24 steps each. The same batch of 98,304 steps is now collected by 16,384 robots with 6 steps each. What changes?
Обучение сходится с трудом: GAE нужны на: Training struggles to converge: GAE needs the rewards of several consecutive steps, and the authors put the limit at 25 steps, half a second
Обучение ускорится: больше роботов — бол: Training speeds up: more robots means more diversity
Ничего: порция та же, а PPO всё равно, к: Nothing: the batch is the same, and PPO doesn't care who collected it
Порция опыта — роботы × шаги подряд. Бол: A rollout batch is robots × consecutive steps. More robots for the same batch means fewer consecutive steps for each; fewer robots means that neighboring steps of one robot are similar to each other. The authors' best compromise is 2,048–4,096 robots and batches of 100,000–200,000 steps. With 4,096 × 24 steps × 1,500 updates, that's 147 million steps, 34 days of one robot's experience in 20 minutes; each copy walks for only 12 minutes.
Сколько шагов симуляции нужно ходьбе: How many simulation steps walking takes
DQN teaches Ada's arm to reach a goal. A transition from the first, almost random episode sits in the buffer. How many times will it get into batches by step 1,000, and what will happen to its target value?
Около 73 раз, и цель r + γ max Q(s′, a′): About 73 times, and its target value r + γ max Q(s′, a′) will drop from −1.35 to −4.98: the record is the same, but the network has learned how many penalized steps lie ahead
Один раз: после первого обновления перех: Once: after the first update, the transition is obsolete
Около 73 раз, но цель останется прежней:: About 73 times, but its target value will stay the same: the record in the buffer doesn't change
Цель Q-обучения не зависит от того, кто: The Q-learning target value doesn't depend on who chose the recorded action, so the Q-function learns from any transition, and that is what makes the buffer possible. When the first transition first got into a batch, the network knew almost nothing, and the target value was almost equal to the reward alone; by step 1,000, the target network knows that from a far-off position, many penalized steps lie ahead.
Q-функция учится на любых переходах: DQN: The Q-function learns from any transitions: DQN and the replay buffer
Ту же DQN учат не на случайных пакетах и: The same DQN is trained not on random batches from the buffer but on the last 32 transitions in a row. What happens to success on the 40 test goals over 1,500 steps?
Средний успех на последних проверках упа: The average success over the last tests drops from 96 to 52%, and the worst test gives 33%: neighboring transitions are similar, and the network gets dragged after the latest situation
Вырастет: свежие переходы описывают теку: It goes up: fresh transitions describe the current policy more accurately
Не изменится: переходов в пакете столько: It doesn't change: the batch holds just as many transitions
Авторы DQN называют три причины для буфе: The DQN authors give three reasons for the buffer: each transition teaches many times, a random batch breaks the correlation between neighboring frames, and averaging over past policies keeps the current weights from deciding which data come next. In the interactive, a buffer of 250 transitions gave 98%, one of 100 gave 69%, and one of 500 gave 100%.
Буфер по шагам: какие переходы попадают: The buffer step by step: which transitions get into training
PPO и SAC учат одну и ту же руку Ады оди: PPO and SAC each train Ada's arm with identical networks. SAC reaches 90% success by interaction step 500, and PPO by step 1,250. Which one is cheaper in compute up to 90%?
Примерно поровну: 118 млн умножений у SA: Roughly even: 118 million multiplications for SAC versus 98 million for PPO; SAC spends three times more per step but needs 2.5 times fewer steps
SAC: быстрее по шагам — значит, и по выч: SAC: faster in steps means faster in compute too
PPO: у него нет двух Q-функций и целевых: PPO: it doesn't have two Q-functions or target copies
SAC экономит шаги, а не вычисления: кажд: SAC saves steps, not compute: it turns every step into an update of two Q-functions and the policy. That is why in simulation, where thousands of robots run in parallel and compute time is expensive, PPO is the usual choice, while on a real robot, where every step is expensive, off-policy methods are. Across eight seeds, SAC reached 90% 2.25–3.75 times sooner in steps.
PPO и SAC на одной руке: успех по шагам: PPO and SAC on the same arm: success by interaction steps
Перед Адой две полки с одинаковыми чашка: In front of Ada are two shelves with identical cups, and the reward is the same at both. SAC trains for 2,000 steps with the temperature α = 1: the bonus for randomness weighs as much as the reward. Where will the 40 attempts end up?
Почти никуда: у полок заканчиваются 3% п: Almost nowhere: only 3% of the attempts end at the shelves; randomness outweighs the reward, and the policy holds on to no strategy
К обеим полкам поровну: награда одинаков: At both shelves equally: the reward is the same, and randomness splits the attempts
К одной полке, как при малой α: награда: At one shelf, as with a small α: the reward wins anyway
Температура — ручка между крайностями. П: The temperature is a knob between two extremes. At α = 0.01, Ada went to one shelf in 98% of the attempts and never tried the other, and at α = 1 she went almost nowhere. The window in which she goes to both is narrow and depends on the seed, so in the second version of SAC α tunes itself, holding the entropy of the policy at the target −dim A: with it, 100% of the attempts went to one shelf, and α dropped to 0.018.
Температура α: одна стратегия, две или н: The temperature α: one strategy, two or none
Две политики руки Ады обучены одним бюдж: Two policies for Ada's arm are trained with the same budget: one in the nominal world, the other with dynamics randomization at width ×1. They are tested in the nominal world, where the first one trained. Which one brings the cup to the target faster?
Политика без рандомизации: 0,49 с против: The policy without randomization: 0.49 s versus 0.55 s; reliability on other arms is paid for with speed
Политика с рандомизацией: она видела бол: The policy with randomization: it has seen more worlds and is more confident
Поровну: в номинальном мире обе удержива: Equally fast: in the nominal world, both hold the cup in 20 attempts out of 20
Политика без памяти не знает, какой мир: A policy without memory doesn't know which world it got, so it picks one cautious behavior for all the training worlds, even where it could go faster. In return, on the six “real” arms it holds the cup in 99% of attempts versus 78%; the policy from the exact world does worst on Ada 4, with 45 ms of latency: 7 attempts out of 20.
С рандомизацией и без: один бюджет, одни: With and without randomization: one budget, the same real arms
Диапазоны рандомизации расширили с ×1 до: The randomization ranges are widened from ×1 to ×3: latency up to 150 ms, the cup up to 1.3 kg, motors from 30% strength. What happens on Ada's six real arms?
Удачных попыток не прибавится (98% проти: Success doesn't improve (98% versus 99%), and the trip to the target takes 23% longer: 0.88 s versus 0.72 s
Успех вырастет: настоящие руки точно ока: Success goes up: the real arms are sure to fall inside the ranges
Успех упадёт: политика не выучит столько: Success drops: the policy can't learn so many different worlds
Миров, где быстрый подход к цели кончает: There are too many worlds where a fast approach to the target ends in oscillation, and the reward pulls the policy toward caution everywhere; Tan et al. saw the same on the Minitaur: “the controllers learn to behave conservatively.” On one of the six seeds, the ×3 policy never learned the task in 12,000 steps: 3 attempts out of 20 even in the nominal world. The width is chosen to match the real spread with a small margin.
Tan и соавторы обучили ходьбу Minitaur в: Tan et al. trained the Minitaur to walk in the Bullet simulator, and the real robot fell immediately. What fixed the transfer?
Модель мотора по измерениям и задержка 1: A motor model fitted to measurements and a latency of 15–19 ms, both added to the simulator: without either of them, the policies didn't work on the robot
Более широкая рандомизация масс и трения: Wider randomization of masses and friction
Больше шагов обучения в том же симулятор: More training steps in the same simulator
То, чего симулятор не умеет вовсе, рандо: Randomizing parameters can't cover what the simulator can't do at all: the real world won't be among the variants. For ANYmal's series elastic actuators, Hwangbo et al. trained an actuator network on 4 minutes of recordings: an error of 0.74 N·m versus 3.55 for the ideal model; with an ideal actuator, the policy couldn't make a single step without falling. In practice, a more accurate model and randomization go together.
Модель привода и задержка: сделать симул: Actuator model and latency: bringing the simulator closer to the robot
ADR на руке Ады начинает с номинального: ADR on Ada's arm starts from the nominal world and moves a boundary outward if at least 80% of the attempts at it succeed. The real arms have latencies of 25–45 ms. Where will the ranges stop by the end of training?
Задержка дорастёт до 75 мс — с запасом н: Latency will grow to 75 ms, with a margin over the real arms; motor strength will stop at 63%: weak motors can't hold a heavy cup
Все диапазоны вырастут до физического пр: All the ranges will grow to their physical limits
Задержка остановится первой: она опаснее: Latency will stop first: it is the most dangerous for the policy
ADR не знает заранее, что важно: он расш: ADR doesn't know in advance what matters: it widens each range as long as the policy copes at its edge, and finds the limit on its own. The curriculum also saves steps: ADR reached 90% on the real arms by step 4,800, and the fixed ×3 range from the first step by step 10,800. At OpenAI, ADR raised transfer from 2.7 to 13.3 cube turns in a row.
ADR на руке Ады: где диапазоны останавли: ADR on Ada's arm: where the ranges stop
Расставь по порядку, как в уроке 5.5 пол: Put in order how lesson 5.5 obtains a speed policy for the real Ada, who doesn't know the traction of the floor.
Учитель: в симуляторе политика, которой: Teacher: in the simulator, a policy that is given the traction μ learns with PPO, 120 updates of 8 drives each
Первые поездки: учитель проезжает 8 поез: First drives: the teacher makes 8 drives, and its speed in every state becomes the answer for the student
Свои поездки: ученик едет сам по датчика: Student's drives: the student drives on its own, from its sensors and history, while the teacher labels every visited state (DAgger), for 5 more iterations
Робот: на настоящей Аде остаётся только: Robot: only the student remains on the real Ada; the teacher and μ stay in the simulator
Lee и соавторам не удалось обучить ходьб: Lee et al. couldn't directly train a policy on the sensors alone to walk over challenging terrain, while a teacher with the terrain and friction as input learned quickly. The student is trained on its own drives: in Learning by Cheating, the student's own drives raised success from 16 to 64%, and in the lab, DAgger gave 100% after 6 iterations versus 48% for copying the teacher's drives.
Учитель, который знает пол: обучение в д: A teacher that knows the floor: training in two stages
Политику скорости Ады учат с подкреплени: Ada's speed policy is trained with reinforcement learning directly on the sensors, without μ and without a teacher. What happens on carpet and on a wet floor?
Доезжает везде, но осторожно: на ковре 6: It makes it everywhere, but cautiously: 6.3 s on carpet versus 5.0 s for the teacher; not knowing the traction, the policy drives as if the floor were wet everywhere
Врезается на мокром полу: без μ ездить п: It crashes on the wet floor: you can't drive on it without μ
Ездит как учитель: награда та же самая: It drives like the teacher: the reward is exactly the same
Авторы RMA пишут о том же: политика, кот: The RMA authors write the same about a policy that doesn't know the parameters of the world: “it learns a very conservative policy which loses on performance”; in their simulation, it scored 62.4% versus 73.5% for RMA. The teacher is needed not for reliability but so that the student knows how to drive on each floor: the student with a history of the last 2 seconds drives like the teacher.
Учитель и два ученика на одном полу: The teacher and two students on the same floor
Ученик без истории на мокром полу не дое: The student without history never makes it on a wet floor. It is switched from copying the teacher's drives to DAgger: it drives by itself, and the teacher labels its states. Will this help?
Нет: 48–60% на всех зёрнах. DAgger чинит: No: 48–60% on all seeds. DAgger fixes distribution shift, not missing information about the floor: the sensors alone can't tell you which floor it is
Да: на своих поездках ученик увидит мокр: Yes: on its own drives, the student will see the wet floor and learn to brake
Да, если итераций будет больше шести: Yes, if there are more than six iterations
В одном и том же месте маршрута учитель: At the same place on the route, the teacher goes at full speed on carpet and brakes on a wet floor: the right answer depends on μ. The student without history learns something in between, too cautious on carpet and too bold on a wet floor, however much you ask the teacher. For the student with history, DAgger gave 100% of test drives versus 48% for copying.
Прогноз: ученик на поездках учителя или: Forecast: the student on the teacher's drives or on its own
Адаптационный модуль оценивает сцепление: The adaptation module estimates traction from the history of the last 2 seconds. Ada drives from carpet into a wet kitchen, and on another drive from a wet floor onto carpet. Which change will the module notice faster?
Мокрую кухню: через 2 шага оценка упала: The wet kitchen: within 2 steps, the estimate dropped from 0.89 to 0.47. The return to carpet comes slowly: in the first second, the estimate averages 0.51
Оба перехода одинаково: история в обе ст: Both changes equally: the history is the same in both directions
Ковёр: хорошее сцепление видно сразу по: The carpet: good traction shows right away in the acceleration
Модуль узнаёт пол из того, как Ада тормо: The module recognizes the floor from how Ada brakes and turns: a slippery floor gives itself away at the very first braking or turn, while on a good floor all you can see is that there is enough traction, as long as the wheels don't slip. Lee et al. saw the same on ANYmal: the friction estimate dropped as soon as the first foot started slipping and rose about 2 seconds after the robot returned to normal ground.
Адаптационный модуль на смене пола: The adaptation module on a change of floor
Обучение по демонстрациям (BC) учится на: Imitation learning (BC) trains on the logs of three operators: 20 drives by the careful one, 40 by the hasty one and 40 by the random one. How will Ada drive?
Медленно в прихожей и гостиной, где чаще: Slowly in the hallway and the living room, where the logged drives were more often slow, and fast in the kitchen, where the hasty operator crashed: 14 drives out of 20 succeed, and all 6 crashes are in the kitchen
Как аккуратный оператор: он единственный: Like the careful operator: the only one who never crashes
Быстро там, где это безопасно, и медленн: Fast where it is safe and slowly in the turn: the best of all the logs
BC копирует самое частое действие логов: BC copies the most frequent logged action at every point and doesn't care how the drive ended. All 40 of the hasty operator's drives got as far as the kitchen, so there BC chooses the fast speed in 89% of decisions. IQL on the same logs does the opposite: fast in the hallway and the living room (59–62%), slow in the kitchen (9%), 18 drives out of 20 and a return of +1.98 versus +0.51 for the best operator.
Четыре политики на одних логах: Four policies on the same logs
Перед проёмом в гостиную наивная Q-функц: In front of the doorway to the living room, the naive Q-function trained on the logs alone rates the action “full left, slow” 12.5 above the most frequent one at this spot. How many such decisions are recorded nearby, and what does this action actually give?
5 из 375, все от случайного оператора; н: 5 of 375, all by the random operator; in reality, +0.01 over the most frequent action
Больше половины: поэтому Q-функция его и: More than half: that's why the Q-function chose it
Ни одного: Q-функция оценивает только не: None: the Q-function only evaluates unrecorded actions
Это оптимизм вне данных: оценка редкого: This is optimism outside the data: nothing checks the estimate of a rare action, and the maximum in the target r + γ max Q picks the most inflated one and carries it over to neighboring states. Online, an attempt would correct such an error; offline, only a penalty can: CQL at α = 0.03 leaves the peak, and Ada never makes it; at α = 0.3 she makes it in 15 drives out of 20, and from α = 1 up, CQL picks the most frequent logged action.
Щуп для Q-функции: что она обещает в одн: A probe for the Q-function: what it promises at a single point
Чем IQL отличается от CQL в обращении с: How does IQL differ from CQL in how it treats actions that aren't in the logs?
IQL их не оценивает вовсе: V(s) — экспек: IQL doesn't evaluate them at all: V(s) is an expectile over the estimates of recorded actions only, the target for Q is r + γV(s′), and the policy copies recorded actions with weights based on the advantage; CQL penalizes high estimates outside the data
IQL запрещает редкие действия по модели: IQL forbids rare actions using an imitation learning model, as BCQ does
Ничем: оба опускают оценки вне данных шт: In no way: both push down estimates outside the data with a penalty, only with different weights
При τ = 0,7 недооценка обходится в 0,7 к: At τ = 0.7, underestimation costs 0.7 of the squared error and overestimation 0.3, so V(s) is pulled toward the best of the recorded actions but doesn't go beyond them. That is why IQL's promise at the start almost matched the outcome: 0.60 versus 0.66, while CQL promised 11.2 against −0.45 in reality, and naive Q-learning 93.0 against −3.92.
Три способа не верить Q-функции вне данн: Three ways not to trust the Q-function outside the data: BCQ, CQL and IQL
IQL учится на 60 поездках одного торопли: IQL trains on 60 drives of the hasty operator alone, who always drives at 80 cm/s and often crashes in the turn into the kitchen. What comes out?
Политика едет всегда быстро и врезается,: The policy always drives fast and crashes just like the operator: it makes it in 8 drives out of 20; there are no slow actions in the logs, so there's nothing to learn braking from
Политика научится тормозить: штраф −5 за: The policy learns to brake: the −5 penalty for a collision shows where to slow down
Политика поедет медленно, как аккуратный: The policy drives slowly, like the careful operator
Offline RL не придумает действий, которы: Offline RL won't invent actions that aren't in the data. On the careful operator's logs, IQL drives like that operator, in 15.1 s; and the logs of the random operator, who reached the kitchen in only 17 drives out of 100, produced the best policy of the lesson: 20 of 20 in 8.2 s and a return of +4.02, because those recordings contain different actions and show what they lead to.
Расставь по порядку, как устроен контур: Put the HIL-SERL loop in order, from preparation to the policy update.
Подготовка: 20–30 демонстраций 3D-мышью: Preparation: 20–30 demonstrations with a 3D mouse and about 5 minutes of recordings for the reward classifier, roughly 200 success frames and 1,000 failure frames
Попытка: робот действует политикой 10 ра: Attempt: the robot acts with the policy 10 times per second, the classifier gives each frame a 0 or a 1, and the steps go into the experience buffer
Перехват: человек берёт 3D-мышь, когда р: Takeover: a person grabs the 3D mouse when the arm is heading into an unrecoverable position, and their steps go into both buffers
Обновление: RLPD берёт пакет наполовину: Update: RLPD draws a batch half from the buffer of demonstrations and corrections and half from experience, and sends the robot new weights
Исправлений мало, но из-за симметричной: There are few corrections, but thanks to symmetric sampling they make up half of every batch, and the policy learns from them right away. On 11 tasks, the policy reached 100% in 1–2.5 hours; HG-DAgger with the same attempts and interventions averaged 49.7%, and 200 demonstrations without interventions gave 0% on the dashboard.

Политику Ады дообучают на одних и тех же: Ada's policy is fine-tuned on the same 100 monitored attempts in three ways: successful attempts only, all attempts with an advantage label in the input, and all attempts unlabeled. Which one gets the cup into the slot fastest?
«Все с меткой»: 13,3 шага против 13,8 у: “All labeled”: 13.3 steps versus 13.8 for “successes only” and 14.6 for “all unlabeled”; of the 1,252 steps in successful attempts, 649 are labeled worse than usual, and the policy doesn't repeat them
«Только удачные»: в ней нет ни одного пл: “Successes only”: it has no bad steps at all
«Все без разметки»: у неё больше всего д: “All unlabeled”: it has the most data
Фильтр по исходу выбрасывает неудачные п: The outcome filter throws out failed attempts whole, while the label tells steps apart within an attempt: of the 149 steps in failed attempts, 56 are labeled positive, namely the beginning of the attempt and the watcher's corrections. Out of 60 starts, the three policies succeed in 59, 56 and 51; the unlabeled policy succeeded in only 1 of 8 starts from the adjacent slot, because it also learns from the moves into the shelf.
Трое на одних попытках: только удачные,: Three ways to learn from the same attempts: successes only, all labeled, all unlabeled
Почему RECAP в π*0.6 записывает преимуще: Why does RECAP in π*0.6 write the advantage into the model's input in words, “Advantage: positive / negative”, instead of using it as an example weight?
Взвешенная регрессия выбрасывает или зан: Weighted regression discards or downweights most of the data and gives slow policies, the policy gradient doesn't get along with flow matching, and a model with the label sees all the data and remains a supervised model
Потому что у VLA нет функции ценности, и: Because a VLA has no value function, so the advantage has to be entered as text
Чтобы оператор мог задавать метку вручну: So that an operator can set the label by hand during work
Ценность в RECAP — минус число шагов до: In RECAP, the value is minus the number of steps to success, learned from the robot's own attempts and predicted as a distribution over 201 bins; the advantage is computed over 50 steps ahead and compared with a task threshold, so that about 40% of attempts get a positive label during fine-tuning. Operator corrections are always labeled positive, and at run time the input always says positive. On the hardest tasks, throughput more than doubled.
RECAP: ценность по собственным попыткам: RECAP: value from the robot's own attempts and the advantage in the model's input
На робота есть 8 минут. Оператор может з: There are 8 minutes of robot time. The operator can record 80 more demonstrations from the home pose, or the robot can make three iterations of 25 monitored attempts, with fine-tuning after each. Which gives more successful starts out of 60?
Опыт с исправлениями: 60 из 60 против 44: Experience with corrections: 60 of 60 versus 44, the same as with the original 40 demonstrations
Демонстрации: они точнее попыток робота: Demonstrations: they are more precise than the robot's noisy attempts
Поровну: 8 минут данных в обоих случаях: Equal: 8 minutes of data either way
Промахи сидят у шкафа и в соседней нише,: The misses happen at the cabinet and in the adjacent slot, while the demonstrations are recorded from the home pose, and examples from there are already plentiful. Even 320 demonstrations over half an hour give 55 of 60 and only 3 of 8 starts from the adjacent slot: the operator's recordings have no backing out. A quarter of an hour of experience with corrections gives 59–60 of 60 and 7–8 of 8 from the slot; in HIL-SERL, 200 demonstrations without interventions gave 0% on the dashboard.

Награда за въезд в клетку у холодильника: A reward for entering the cell by the fridge is a loophole: the state “cell” doesn't remember whether the milk has been picked up, so Ada gets paid for it again and again. While the reward is small, the stop at the fridge doesn't pay off, and as soon as it does, Ada is better off shuttling between the fridge and the neighboring cell, and the episode never ends, whatever the reward. For the reward to be paid once, the state has to include whether Ada has the milk: there are 142 states instead of 71, and value iteration computes them the same way. Then the reward has to pay for six extra steps, and the smaller γ is, the larger it must be: for a reward at the moment of pickup, ${thText('once')}; for a reward at the stove together with the milk, ${thText('atgoal')}. Sutton and Barto's rule: reward the win, not the captured pieces.
